full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the judgment and order dated 16-10-1993 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Dinajpur in Criminal Appeal No. 14 of 1981 dismissing the appeal and upholding the judgment and order dated 3-4-1981 passed by the Assistant Sessions Judge, Dinajpur in Session Case No. 542 of 1979 convicting the accused petitioner Maniruzzaman alias Md Maniruzzaman under section 471 of the Penal Code and sentencing him thereunder to suffer RI for four years and convicting co-accused Akbor Ali under sections 471/34 of the Penal Code and sentencing him thereunder to suffer RI for four years. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that, accused Md Maniruzzaman and two others in collusion with each other created a forged and fabricated Power of Attorney in the name of Mahabir Prosad Roy purportedly appointing accused Akbor Ali and Ashraf Ali as his constituted attorneys in his name on his behalf authorising them to execute deeds of exchange for lands situated in Bangladesh (previously East Pakistan) described in schedule-A to the Power of Attorney against the lands owned and possessed by accused Maniruzzaman in West Dinajpur in India, described in schedule-''B'' of the deed concerned. On the basis of the aforesaid forged and fabricated Power of Attorney the accused persons filed a Miscellaneous Case before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), Dinajpur praying for permission for executing deeds of exchange in respect of the case property. The learned Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Rev)) sensed foul-play in the matter and referred the case to the Bureau of Anti-Corruption for taking necessary action. An officer of the Bureau of Anti-Corruption accordingly, inquired into the matter and found that the so-called Power of Attorney by Mohabir Prashad Roy is false and fabricated whereupon he started a regular case against the accused after lodging an FIR at the local police station. An Inspector of the Bureau of Anti-Corruption investigated the case, examined witnesses, seized alamats and recorded the statement of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and on completion of the investigation submitted charge sheet against the three accused persons under sections 467/34 and 471/34 of the Penal Code. 

 3. Upon the aforesaid allegations accused petitioner Maniruzzaman alias Md Maniruzzaman and two other co-accused were put on trial before the Assistant Sessions Judge, Dinajpur in Session Case No. 542 of 1989 to answer charges under sections 467/34 and 471/34 of the Penal Code to which they pleaded not guilty and contended, inter alia, that they have been falsely implicated in the case at the instance of the same designing persons. 

 4. At the trial the prosecution examined 13 witnesses, including formal witnesses, and exhibited a series of documents in support of its case while the defence examined none. The learned Assistant Sessions Judge by his impugned judgment dated 3-4-1991 found petitioner Maniruzzaman and co-accused Akbor Ali guilty under sections 471/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced them thereunder to suffer RI for four years and acquitted co-accused Ashraf Ali of the charges levelled against him. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Assistant Sessions Judge, accused petitioner Maniruzzaman and co-accused Akbor Ali took an appeal before the Sessions Judge, Dinajpur being Criminal Appeal No. 14 of 1987, and the learned Additional Sessions Judge, who heard the appeal, eventually dismissed the appeal and upheld the order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned trial Court. It is against this judgment accused petitioner Maniruzzaman moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 7. PW 1 Inspector Farahjul Huq of the Bureau of Anti-Corruption is the informant as well as the Investigating Officer of the case. He stated in his evidence that Mahabir Prashad Roy did not execute the alleged Power of Attorney in favour of the accused persons and he never exchanged his Bangladesh properties with those of the accused persons in India. He also stated that Mahabir Prashad Roy died in this country on 26th Bhadra 1372 BS. He also stated that Mahabir Prashad Roy duly executed a registered deed of exchange dated 22-7-65 in respect of some of his properties and he seized the said deed of exchange, which has been marked as an exhibit in the case. He also stated that by creating a false Power of Attorney in the name of Mahabir Prashad Roy, the accused attempted to obtain permission from ADC (Rev) to execute deeds of exchange in respect of the case property to illegally grab the case property and to that end they filled an application before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) praying for legalising the exchange. 

 8. PW No. 2 Arnapurna Debi, wife of Mahabir Prashad Roy, stated in her evidence that her husband Mahabir Prashad Roy never executed any Power of Attorney in favour of the accused persons and he never exchanged any land with them at any point of time. She further stated that her husband Mahabir Prashad Roy duly executed a deed of exchange with one Ahima Bewa on 22-7-65 in respect of some of his lands. She further stated that after creating false and fictitious Power of Attorney in the name of her husband the accused filed a miscellaneous case before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) Dinajpur for legalising a fake exchange and after coming to learn about it she duly filed an objection in the case whereupon the learned Additional Deputy Commissioner referred the matter to the Bureau of Anti-Corruption for necessary action. 

 10. PW No. 4 Md Syedur Rahman stated in his evidence that he filed written objection before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), Dinajpur in connection with the miscellaneous case for resisting the proposed exchange on the basis of a forged and fictitious Power of Attorney. He figured as a witness in the seizure list by which the Investigating Officer seized papers relating to the marriage of Arna Punta Debi with Mahabir Prashad Roy. 

 18. PW 13 stated in his evidence that he looked after the case of PW 2 Arnapurna Debi before ADC (Rev), Dinajpur. He stated that he personally knew Mahabir Prashad who died in this country. 

 19. From the scrutiny of the evidence discussed above, I find that the prosecution has been able to prove by most convincing and satisfactory evidence that the alleged Power of Attorney by Mahabir Prashad Roy in favour of the accused persons is a forged and fabricated document and the, accused persons used the said forged document before the ADC (Rev), Dinajpur in their bid to legalise their fake exchange knowing full well that the so-called Power of Attorney by Mahabir Prashad Roy is a false and fictitious one. The learned trial Court as well as the learned Court of appeal below duly considered all the relevant aspects of the case and the evidence on record and I do not find any impropriety and infirmity in the impugned order of conviction and sentence passed against the accused persons. The learned Courts below duly considered the defence case in its true perspective and rightly rejected the same on assigning cogent reasons. 

 20. In the revisional application the petitioner raised a question on section 195 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and contended that since the disputed Power of Attorney was produced before the ADC (Rev.), Dinajpur in connection with the Miscellaneous Case for legalising it, section 195 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is a bar against his prosecution in the absence of any written complaint by the ADC (Rev), Dinajpur. In this connection it is to be pointed out that the ADC (Rev), Dinajpur was dealing with the exchange case in his administrative capacity and not as a Court within the meaning of section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In order to constitute a Court in the true sense of the term an essential condition is that the Court or Tribunal must have the necessary trappings of a judicial entity and the power to give a decision of a definitive judicial nature and putting the seal of finality and authoritativeness to the matter. While exercising judicial powers the Court or Tribunal as a part of the judicial machinery of the country determines the rights of the subjects according to established judicial norms and procedure laid down in the statutes but an officer dealing with a miscellaneous case regarding exchange of properties merely acts as an executive authority and does not act as a judicial machinery nor is he invested with any of the judicial powers as such. Consequently, there is no substance in the defence plea and in the absence of any written complaint from the ADC (Rev), Dinajpur the present criminal case is hit by the provisions of section 195 (1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Moreover, in this case, it is evident that the Bureau of Anti-Corruption took up the case for enquiry on a written reference from the ADC (Rev), Dinajpur which is, in fact, a written complaint and this dispels all notions about the question of maintainability of the present criminal case and the alleged bar under section 195)(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. For the reasons stated above, I am of the view that the learned Courts below were perfectly justified in convicting and sentencing the accused petitioner under sections 471/34 of the Penal Code and the impugned judgments do not call for any interference by this Court exercising revisional power under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 21. In the result, this Rule is discharged. The impugned order of conviction and sentence dated 3-4-1989 passed by the Assistant Sessions Judge, Dinajpur in Session Case No. 542 of 1979 under sections 471/34 of the Penal Code, which has been affirmed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Dinajpur in Criminal Appeal No. 14 of 1981, is maintained. The accused petitioner Md Maniruzzaman, who is presently on bail, is directed to surrender to his bail bonds immediately to serve out the sentence imposed upon him.
